mainEntity.name: What is fractional PR for an AI startup?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fractional PR for an AI startup is a senior PR operator working directly with the founder or CMO on a part-time retainer, in place of a full agency. The operator handles narrative direction, journalist outreach to Tier-1 outlets (Forbes, AI Magazine, Decrypt, The Information, TechCrunch), founder profiling, op-ed ghostwriting, and podcast bookings. For AI startups pre-Series B, this typically replaces a $25,000 to $50,000 per month agency retainer with $5,000 to $12,000 per month for the same scope, because there is no account-team layer to fund.

mainEntity.name: How is PR for AI startups different from generic tech PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three differences. First, the journalist map is narrower and more specific: AI Magazine, The Information, Forbes AI, Decrypt AI, Bloomberg Tech, plus a handful of named beat reporters at TechCrunch and Wired. Second, the narrative cycle moves on category creation, not feature releases: an AI founder profiled as a category voice (the Stripe for AI agents, the Linear for AI workflows) compounds; a generic product announcement decays in 48 hours. Third, AI Overviews and Perplexity now cite AI-startup pages at a higher rate than generic tech pages because the topic is queried more often, which means schema, FAQ structure, and named-author bylines move citation share materially.

mainEntity.name: What does an AI startup PR engagement look like in the first 90 days?

acceptedAnswer.text: Days 1 to 14: positioning audit, narrative thesis, journalist mapping, embargo and announcement calendar. Days 15 to 45: founder profiling sprint (LinkedIn rebuild, X cadence, 2 op-ed drafts, 4 podcast bookings) and first Tier-1 placement around an existing news hook. Days 46 to 90: cadence of 2 to 4 Tier-1 placements per month at steady state, op-ed of the month, podcast tour, KOL coordination across X dev community and AI YouTube creators. Reporting is weekly, asynchronous, and uses real placement data, not vanity metrics.

mainEntity.name: How much does PR for an AI startup cost in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fractional senior PR for an AI startup in 2026 runs $5,000 to $12,000 per month. A traditional AI-PR agency (Mission North, Highwire, Method, Bospar) charges $20,000 to $50,000 per month for the same Tier-1 scope, because the retainer funds a 5-person account team. Single-launch sprints (4 to 6 weeks around a Series A, model release, or partnership announcement) range from $15,000 to $40,000. The pricing model that fits 80 percent of AI startups pre-Series B is a 3 to 6 month fractional retainer with a launch sprint stacked on top of the announcement window.

mainEntity.name: Can you place an AI startup in Forbes or The Information?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, when the story fits. The Gaia AI campaign in 2025 placed the protocol in Forbes (covered as 'the Stripe for AI agents'), Decrypt, and Benzinga in a single news cycle. Forbes responds to category-defining narratives, named founders with verifiable track records, and clear technical differentiation. The Information responds to deeply-reported angles with internal documents or first-mover positioning. Neither responds to generic press releases. The work is in the narrative thesis and the named anchor reporters, not in the pitch volume.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with seed-stage AI startups or only Series A and later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Seed-stage AI startups get the most leverage from a focused 8 to 12 week fractional engagement rather than a 12-month retainer. The scope is narrower: positioning thesis, one Tier-1 placement around the funding announcement, founder LinkedIn and X build, and 3 podcast bookings. After Series A, the same operator transitions into an ongoing retainer with category-creation work as the core deliverable. Pre-seed and very early seed without a product or named pilot customer usually does not yet need PR; the budget is better spent on product.

mainEntity.name: How does AI startup PR work in Korea in 2026 (named outlets, AI policy frame, KBW AI track)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Korean AI press cycles run through a narrower outlet set than crypto: ChosunBiz AI desk, ZDNet Korea, Electronic Times (Etnews), Maeil Business AI, and the AI section of BloomingBit for crypto-adjacent AI. The policy frame is the Personal Information Protection Commission AI guidance, the Ministry of Science and ICT National AI Strategy, and the K-AI Sovereignty narrative the government uses to filter foreign-AI coverage. KBW 2026 (September 22 to 28, COEX) added a dedicated AI track in 2025; Korean editors expect a named ROK enterprise pilot before they take a tier-1 brief, not a US logo list. Naver Search Generative Experience cites Korean-original AI commentary at materially higher rates than translated Western posts, so the founder needs at least one Korean-original ChosunBiz or Maeil byline before the AI Overviews citation graph picks up the entity.

mainEntity.name: How does AI startup PR work in Japan in 2026 (Nikkei Cross Tech, METI, WebX AI, note.com)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Japanese AI press anchors on Nikkei Cross Tech, ITmedia AI+, Impress Watch, ASCII.jp and the Nikkei Asia AI desk for cross-border angles. The policy frame is the METI AI Guidelines for Business, the Cabinet Office AI Strategy 2026, and the Hiroshima AI Process G7 framework — Japanese editors weigh AI vendors against that frame, not against the US Executive Order frame. note.com is the highest-leverage long-form citation surface in Japan and Perplexity Japanese-language citation share concentrates there, so a founder essay on note.com translates into AI-Overviews and Perplexity citations inside 30 days. WebX 2026 (July 13 to 14, Tokyo) added an AI summit track; for Japanese tier-1, the named enterprise pilot (Mitsubishi, NTT, SoftBank Robotics, Rakuten) outranks the US customer logo every time.

mainEntity.name: How does AI startup PR work in Singapore in 2026 (e27, Tech in Asia, IMDA Model AI, Token2049 AI)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Singapore AI press runs through e27, Tech in Asia, DealStreetAsia, The Business Times tech desk and CNA Insider for category-defining angles. The policy frame is the IMDA Model AI Governance Framework v2 and the AI Verify testing toolkit — Singapore editors and the Smart Nation buyer set expect alignment with that frame, not US Executive Order language. Project Moonshot (IMDA AI safety testing initiative) is the credibility anchor for AI Verify-aligned vendors. The Token2049 Singapore (October, Marina Bay Sands) AI track is the institutional-allocator press cycle for AI-meets-crypto; SuperAI Singapore (June, Marina Bay Sands) is the AI-pure cycle. Without an MAS or AI Verify tie, top-tier Singapore editors treat the brief as a US founder doing English-language SEO, not a regional category-creation play.

mainEntity.name: How does AI startup PR work in Dubai and MENA in 2026 (Arabian Business, GITEX AI, UAE AI Strategy 2031)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dubai and MENA AI press runs through Arabian Business, Gulf News tech desk, The National tech, Forbes Middle East AI list, Wamda for startup angles and Asharq Business for Arabic-language depth. The policy frame is the UAE AI Strategy 2031, the Ministry of AI portfolio under HE Omar Sultan Al Olama, and the Falcon LLM (TII) sovereign-AI narrative — regional editors weigh foreign AI founders against that frame. GITEX Global 2026 (October, Dubai World Trade Centre) added a dedicated AI Everything pavilion; for tier-1 coverage the editor wants a named UAE pilot (PIF, Mubadala, ADQ, G42-adjacent) before the desk takes the brief. Arabic-language Asharq Business and Cointelegraph Arabic AI desk are the LLM citation surfaces ChatGPT and Claude reach for on Arabic-language buyer queries — without Arabic-original coverage, the AI Overviews entity graph stays English-only.

mainEntity.name: How does AI startup PR work in India in 2026 (Inc42, ET Tech, IndiaAI Mission, ETHIndia AI)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Indian AI press anchors on Inc42 AI desk, ET Tech, YourStory AI, MoneyControl Tech, Forbes India AI list and Analytics India Magazine for technical depth. The policy frame is the IndiaAI Mission (Ministry of Electronics and IT, $1.25B program), the Digital India Bhashini language-AI initiative, and the DPDP Act 2023 data-protection layer — Indian editors expect IndiaAI Mission alignment over US-Executive-Order framing. The IndiaAI Compute Portal sovereign-GPU layer is the credibility frame for infrastructure AI; Bhashini is the credibility frame for multilingual or applied AI. ETHIndia (December, Bengaluru) and Cypher India by Analytics India (September) are the named-builder convergence cycles. Hindi-original coverage in Dainik Bhaskar Tech or Aaj Tak Tech moves Perplexity Hindi-language citation share materially; English-only coverage caps the AI-Overviews entity graph at the urban-English buyer set.
